newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says does not intend to increase VAT rates.
newsitem.headline: Spain says does not intend to increase VAT rates.

text.p: Spain's Economy Ministry does not intend to hike value-added tax (VAT) from its current 16 percent level, a spokeswoman at the Exchequer said on Monday.
She denied a report in financial newspaper Cinco Dias that the government was studying a possible increase in VAT in 1998 in order to offset either social security contributions or income tax cuts.
"This possibility is not under examination," the spokeswoman told Reuters. "VAT rates will remain where they are next year".
The newpaper showed a table according to which Spanish VAT rates, with the regular one at 16 percent, are jointly with Luxembourg the lowest in Europe.
Cinco Dias said recent progress in limiting consumer price inflation gave the government the possibility of hiking VAT.
